questions.q: A Direct Lake semantic model's report performance degrades noticeably after a large data load. What's the most likely cause?
options: Direct Lake Mode silently fell back to DirectQuery because the table exceeded its size or row-group limits
The Fabric capacity was deleted
Direct Lake Mode always fails outright when data grows, with an error
OneLake stopped storing the table's data
questions.explain: Direct Lake Mode's fallback to DirectQuery is silent, not an error — the single highest-yield performance fact in Domain 3.

questions.q: Where would you go in Fabric to see run history and duration for every pipeline, notebook, and Dataflow in a workspace?
options: The Monitoring Hub
The Git integration panel
The capacity settings page
The OneLake file explorer
questions.explain: The Monitoring Hub (Fabric Lesson 16) is the workspace-wide view for diagnosing exactly this kind of slowdown.

questions.q: A workspace's jobs are queuing and slowing down specifically during peak hours. What should you check first?
options: Capacity utilization — the workspace may be undersized for its SKU
Whether Git integration is enabled
Whether the Lakehouse has a Shortcut
The semantic model's title
questions.explain: Capacity throttling from an undersized SKU (Fabric Lesson 14) is the standard first check for peak-hour job queuing.

questions.q: On DP-700, how does root-cause analysis typically get tested, compared to the full process from Fabric Lesson 58?
options: As a scenario describing symptoms, asking for the single correct next diagnostic step
As an essay question requiring the full incident-response playbook
It is not tested on DP-700 at all
As a request to write a post-mortem document
questions.explain: DP-700 scopes root-cause analysis down to picking the one right next move, not the entire reproduce/isolate/hypothesize/verify cycle.

questions.q: What does Direct Lake Mode do differently from a traditional Import or DirectQuery connection, when it's working as intended?
options: It reads Delta files directly from OneLake without a separate import step or DirectQuery round trip
It copies all data into Power BI's internal storage every refresh
It requires a dedicated SQL endpoint for every query
It disables all Row-Level Security
questions.explain: Direct Lake Mode (Fabric Lesson 12) reads OneLake's Delta files in place, which is what makes its fallback behavior worth knowing.
